statement: Current is the amount of charge stored in the wire, not a rate of flow.
contrast_quote: Current is the rate of flow of charge.

statement: An ammeter is connected in parallel, across the component.
contrast_quote: An ammeter must be connected in series with the component, so that all of the current flows through it.

statement: Current can still flow and light the bulb when the circuit has a gap, because the current just goes to the bulb.
contrast_quote: Current flows only in a complete circuit.

statement: Potential difference flows through the wires, like current does.
contrast_quote: Potential difference is always measured between two points. It does not flow through a wire.

statement: A voltmeter is connected in series, like an ammeter.
contrast_quote: A voltmeter must be connected in parallel, across the component being measured.

statement: Voltage is the same thing as energy, so a 12 V cell gives 12 J whatever the amount of charge.
contrast_quote: A potential difference of one volt means one joule of energy for each coulomb of charge.

statement: A thicker wire has more resistance, because there is more material in the way.
contrast_quote: A thicker wire has a smaller resistance than a thinner wire of the same material and length.

statement: A hotter metal wire lets charge through more easily, so its resistance falls.
contrast_quote: The resistance of a metal wire rises when the wire gets hotter

statement: The resistance of a wire changes whenever the voltage or the current changes.
contrast_quote: For a metal wire at constant temperature, the resistance stays the same whatever the potential difference across it or the current through it.

statement: A larger resistance gives a larger current for the same potential difference.
contrast_quote: When the potential difference stays constant, doubling the resistance halves the current.

statement: Doubling the potential difference doubles the resistance, so the current stays the same.
contrast_quote: When the resistance stays constant, doubling the potential difference doubles the current.

statement: The current against potential difference graph of a filament bulb is a straight line, like a wire.
contrast_quote: The graph for a filament bulb is a curve

statement: Current is used up as it passes through each component, so it is smaller after each bulb.
contrast_quote: The current is the same at every point in a series circuit

statement: Current divides between the components in a series circuit, like water splitting into branches.
contrast_quote: In a series circuit there is only one path for the charge.

statement: Each component in a series circuit gets the full potential difference of the cell.
contrast_quote: The potential differences across the components add up to the potential difference of the supply: V total = V1 + V2 + V3.
